### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6440802ae380f3de266b6d61ecdd0deb9e37f9e3`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **246** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **181** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **181**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **122** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **41** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6440802ae380f3de266b6d61ecdd0deb9e37f9e3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `889ddca9152e0838bee816d52d137aa41fd99584` — the merge of head `aa61f0b261c6dc8d8c2717b1c8b6bb82f20ddfd8` into base `6440802ae380f3de266b6d61ecdd0deb9e37f9e3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 889ddca9152e0838bee816d52d137aa41fd99584 && git checkout 889ddca9152e0838bee816d52d137aa41fd99584
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6440802ae380f3de266b6d61ecdd0deb9e37f9e3 aa61f0b261c6dc8d8c2717b1c8b6bb82f20ddfd8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6440802ae380f3de266b6d61ecdd0deb9e37f9e3 && git merge --no-ff aa61f0b261c6dc8d8c2717b1c8b6bb82f20ddfd8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6440802ae380f3de266b6d61ecdd0deb9e37f9e3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6440802ae380f3de266b6d61ecdd0deb9e37f9e3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Epic red-line review of #32098 (Fixes #32072) at head 04b67d43: PASS on code. The PASS holds once the declaration is corrected on a text-only head.**

- **Red lines 1 and 2: hold.**
  - The query door reads `datasetName` through the protocol's D3 `getMetaItem`. `list.find` is gone, and `?package=` is the `/meta` exact qualifier.
  - `query_dataset` resolves through core `resolvePackageScopedHolders` with no caller: two holders answer 409 naming both, and nothing is picked.
  - A composition with no `getMetaItem` answers `503`, which is fail-closed, in line with #32076.

- **Red line 3: holds on behaviour.** All nine one-holder answers are byte-identical to base ff04ad81. Three ablation legs went red, and the forced edits are named.
- **Red line 3 (d), the declaration: must be corrected** (seat 3 amendment 6760759721). The PR moves three answers from 200 to 409: the bare `/meta/dataset` read, the query door and `query_dataset`, each with two holders. Under G1's precedent (#32097, #32092) that is `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, with FROM→TO for each of the three and the ADR-0087 marker. The `?package=` parameter is the additive half, described in prose. Only the body and the changeset change.
- **Build probes.** When two holders exist, `readItem('dataset')` now swallows the 409 and stops probing. Silence is not a guess, but the operator cannot see it. Have the probe report "not probed: N holders (A, B)" as a warning line in this PR, or say in the body why that is impossible.

These are out of scope and recorded only:
- the UI carrying the package, which is #32077;
- a qualified spelling in the tool input, recorded in the body;
- the agent's own package as the caller of `query_dataset`, which needs the tool context to carry it, after the stop.

epic:#31527#1 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzj7TEH65FDimZdn1H3

**Epic rulings on seat 3's three escalations from the #32098 contract review (bab09042).** ⛔ Not a claim.

1. **S2, `query_dataset`: admission comes first, then D3 over the admitted holders.** ADR-0149 D2 says a hidden dataset and a missing one get the same single NOT_FOUND. If the tool resolves before admission, a 409 naming a holder the caller may not see breaks D2, and so does a 409 whose existence alone tells a one-holder caller about the other. So:
   - The candidates are the holders the caller is admitted to (`admitDatasetCatalogEntry`).
   - **None admitted:** NOT_FOUND, exactly as for a missing name.
   - **Two or more admitted:** 409, naming only the admitted ones.
   - **Exactly one admitted:** that one. That is not a guess under red line 2: a caller cannot mean a dataset it cannot address, and to it the hidden holder does not exist.
   - **Pins:** admitted to neither gets NOT_FOUND, byte-equal to a missing name. Admitted to one gets that one, and no answer names the other. Admitted to both gets 409 naming both.
   - This is not "accepted under Q2 = A": Q2 did not weigh D2. The REST query door follows the same order where it applies admission.
2. **The two holder sets: the served list is the right one, and the gap gets a follow-up.** A disabled package is not a holder an address can reach, so the REST door counting it (the registry) is the outlier. #32101's review found the same class (F4). Not blocking for #32098: both answers fail closed, and the PR body records the difference. Seat 3 files one server-lane p1 card for the class: "by-name doors judge holders over the registry, which counts a disabled package". Scope is every door that asks `packageScopedHoldersOf` / the registry for holders while the served list withholds a disabled package, with a census first. It is attached to #31527.
3. **#31700 carries both probe items. Agreed.** The dataset build probe reads with the publishing package as caller, and the `widget_not_probed` fix text stops prescribing "keep one dataset" once #31700 lets two namespaces hold the name (prescribe the qualified address instead). They are preconditions on #31700, beside 6761712849 and 6764753986.

epic:#31527#1 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzj7TEH65FDimZdn1H3

**Epic red-line read of #32098's delta 78c27dab: PASS. It follows my admission-first ruling 6766102988.** I read the diff and its pins, but did not run them. Contract review and ACCEPT stay with seat 3.

`query_dataset` now checks admission for each holder before it resolves the name, through `savedHoldersOf` and then `resolveAdmittedDataset`:
- **Admitted to no holder:** `NOT_FOUND`, byte-equal to the answer for a name nothing holds, and no holder is named. Pinned.
- **Admitted to one holder:** that holder is served whatever the list order, and the hidden holder is never named. Pinned.
- **Admitted to two of three holders:** `409` naming only those two. Pinned.
- **Fail-closed branches.** An unresolved admission, or a degraded read (`partial: true`), with fewer than two holders admitted answers `503`. It never answers a 404 or picks a holder. With two or more admitted, it refuses as above. This is right: when a holder may be missing, neither "one holder" nor "not found" can be known. Pinned.
- **One holder with several rows** (an overlay beside the composite) is one holder. Before, this threw an undeclared `TypeError`. Now it is served that holder's row, as the old `find` served it. Pinned.
- **An item the parse leaves out is no candidate.** I accept this under the same ruling: no caller can query it, so it is a holder admitted to none. It is declared as item 7.
- **Other changes.** The query door also recognises a refusal by its shape, as in #32117. Items 7 and 10 of the changeset declare the FROM→TO moves. With one holder, the answer is unchanged.

All three red lines hold.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3c68b409e6cc6a554285017c613f8fc1ae0e753a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/build-probes-dataset-holders.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-e8-readers.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/dataset-package-scoped-readers.dogfood.test.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-routes.test.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-16019-driver-declared-fault.test.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-ai-tools-parity.test.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-body-door.test.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-dataset-row-wildcard-door.test.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-tools.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/dataset-tools.test.ts + packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts (`resolvePackageScopedHolders`, `packageScopedHolderSource`), packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts (`isPackageScopedRefusal`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`resolveItem`, `getPackageScopedItem`), docs/adr/0150 (D3 (a), (c)), docs/adr/0149 (D2). Prose faces judged in ②: .changeset/32072-dataset-resolve-by-package.md, content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx.

This is a delta review of bab09042 → 3c68b409: the fix commit 78c27dab, then a merge of `origin/main` at 8523ef9a. Everything the delta does not touch stands as judged in the record on bab09042. Read: the fix commit's diff, the merge result against the old net diff, the PR title and body as they are now, os-dev-report 6767628248, epic ruling 6766102988 and epic delta read 6767366584 (inputs, not adopted), and the 57 check-runs on this head (40 success, 17 skipped, 0 failed). The dogfood shards are still skipped on a PR run by CI design, so the dogfood file's first gate verdict is the queue run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`query_dataset`, admission first: right against ruling 6766102988.** `savedHoldersOf` groups the listed rows of the name by holder. Each holder's item goes through `admitDatasetCatalogEntry`, and `resolveAdmittedDataset` runs core `resolvePackageScopedHolders` over the admitted map only.
  - None admitted: the same `notFound()` a missing name gets, pinned byte-equal.
  - One admitted: served in either list order.
  - Two or more admitted: 409, with the refusal's sentence and `candidates` built from the admitted holders alone.
- **The hidden holder is absent from every answer.** I read each exit:
  - the NOT_FOUND carries the name only;
  - the 409 is built from the admitted source;
  - the unresolved 503 carries the name only;
  - the degraded 503 carries the name and the host's own warning text;
  - a served answer's provenance is the admitted dataset's.
- **Fail-closed 503s: right, and neither leaks against ADR-0149 D2.**
  - The degraded-read 503 fires for every name with fewer than two admitted holders, held or not, so it cannot tell a hidden holder from a missing name.
  - The unresolved 503 fires only when some holder's admission could not be judged. That is the shape ADR-0149 D2 already lists and `main` already answers for a one-holder name. A holder that was judged and denied never produces it: denied alone is NOT_FOUND, and denied beside one admitted serves the admitted one.
- **One holder's rows collapse to its first parsed row: right, not a refusal.** D3 picks among holders. Two rows of one holder are not an ambiguity of the name, and a refusal would be a new narrowing with no remedy the caller could apply. The collapse returns exactly the row the old `find` returned, so the one-holder answer does not move. The residual is S9.
- **The door's shape predicate: equal to the runtime's, no broader.** `isPackageScopedRefusal` in `analytics-routes.ts` is the same three conditions as `runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` (class, or `code === 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'` with `refusal.status === 'refused'`). A shape match is rethrown as core's class over the thrown `refusal`, so the catch's ADR-0112 arm answers 409. Pinned with a plain object.
- **A parse-failed holder is no candidate: accepted under the ruling.** No caller can query it and `list_datasets` never lists it. The forced pin change is named in the dev report and declared in item 7. Against `main` the answer is unchanged, since the old `find` skipped it too.

### ② Semver level

- **Level and lines: unchanged and correct.** `patch` on the four packages, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line-initial in the changeset and the PR body, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and one ADR-0087 marker in each. `Check Changeset` and the lint gates are green on this head.
- **M1: closed.** Items 5 and 6 of the changeset's BREAKING list and of the PR body's FROM → TO section declare the two package-caller narrowings. Each names `SchemaRegistry.resolveItem` and `MetadataFacade.get`, gives FROM served TO `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (`outside-closure`), and carries a one-line fix. The reason code and the D3 (a) / (c) labels match core and the ADR. The `Narrowing:` line names both.
- **S6: closed.** Item 8 declares the list-only protocol 200 → 503. Item 9 declares the repeated `?package=` 400, on both body shapes.
- **S7: closed.** The PR title now carries `!` and `metadata-protocol`.
- **S8: closed in the diff.** The `loadDatasets` jsdoc no longer says the REST door reads the list. The same stale sentence still stands in `runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` and `mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`, outside the diff (nit).
- **N1, N2: closed.** Item 2 names `getMetaItem` beside `GET`. `analytics.mdx` now says 409 when someone holds the name and 404 when nothing does.
- **New moves in the delta: declared, with one gap.** Item 7 (admission first, parse-failed holder) and item 10 (degraded read) are declared with FROM → TO.
